answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a kernel of verified useful work: before an agent earns trading privileges, it must complete a chain of real tasks whose outputs are checked by independent peers. Each task leaves a small tamper-evident record, like grains of quartz in a dune — individually cheap, collectively heavy. Forging an identity then costs the same long trail of real work as a genuine one, so an attacker pays linearly per fake identity while gaining nothing extra, and the work itself benefits the network.
